AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Despite the generalized use of prophylactic antibiotics in orthopaedic surgery, Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) are still a major source of morbidity, mortality, and hospital cost. This is due in part to the increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistant organisms.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A review of local epidemiology, the importance of an antibiotic stewardship program, patient optimization, and risk stratification options to reduce SSIs.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The proportion of revisions due to infection is projected to rise rapidly over the next 25 years. The economic burden of infections is expected to exceed 50% of the inpatient resources available for revision arthroplasties in 2016 total hip arthroplasty (THA) and 2030 total knee arthroplasty (TKA).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Appropriate evidence-based epidemiological strategies must be implemented to reduce SSIs.

Article.ArticleTitle: Decreasing the Incidence of Surgical Site Infections Following Joint Replacement Surgery.

Journal.Title: Bulletin of the Hospital for Joint Disease (2013)
